task: Translate these English strings into Hindi (hi) and Telugu (te) for the school-13-17 audience.

strings.hook.text: A message arrives: “You WON a prize!!! Click now.” Your phone moved it to <term-junk>junk</term-junk> before you ever saw it. No person read it first.
strings.hook.q: So how did a <term-program>program</term-program> decide, about a message it had never seen before?
strings.sort.instruction: Here are eight messages. Sort them into two groups. You are the <term-filter>filter</term-filter> now.
strings.sort.reveal: Look at what you used to decide: money you didn’t expect, words like FREE and URGENT, lots of “!!!”. Those are clues.
strings.knob.prompt: Here is a tiny filter. It counts three kinds of clue in a message and adds up points. Money words are words about getting or paying money: won, prize, free, pay, fee. Urgent words hurry you: urgent, now, only today.
strings.knob.sentence: This message has {excl, plural, one {# “!” mark} other {# “!” marks}}, {money, plural, one {# money word} other {# money words}} and {urgent, plural, one {# urgent word} other {# urgent words}}. Its junk score is {output}, so it goes to {decision}.
strings.knob.success: Score 10: exactly on the threshold, and 10 is enough to go to junk. One point fewer and it reaches the <term-inbox>inbox</term-inbox>.
strings.bh.intro: The filter’s rule is short. Below, each message shows its clues and their points: 1 for each “!”, 2 for each money word, 3 for each urgent word. Your job: add up the points, compare the total with 10, and choose Junk or Inbox. Do two by hand, then let the machine do the rest.
strings.bh.rule: If a message’s score is {threshold} or more, it goes to junk. Otherwise it goes to the inbox.
strings.bh.auto: The machine did the same step, the same way, every time. It cannot get tired, and it has no common sense to fall back on: it only follows the steps. So two scams, the locked-account message and the pay-a-fee message, slipped into the inbox.
strings.cmp.explain: Only the “!” marks changed. The excited version has 10 of them, 1 point each, so its score is 10: it reached the threshold. A real message from a friend lands in junk. The filter cannot tell an excited friend from a scammer. It only counts.
strings.an.break: Here the comparison stops working. An examiner reads your answers and understands them. The filter only counts clues. It has no idea what a message means.
strings.deep.text: Real filters often use hundreds of clues, not three. Their points are usually not set by hand: the filter works them out from millions of messages that people marked as junk or as real. That is called <term-training>training</term-training>.
strings.deepest.text: Choosing the threshold is a trade-off. A low threshold catches more junk but also blocks more real messages. A high threshold lets real messages through but lets more junk in too. There is no setting that makes zero mistakes.
strings.yd.prompt: Make up to five messages that you think would fool this filter. Use made-up words only: no real names or phone numbers. For each one, work out its score: 1 point for each “!”, 2 for each money word, 3 for each urgent word. Would it reach 10?
strings.ch.f1: Its score is 0, because it has no clues. Is 0 at least 10?
strings.br.r1: The filter no longer sees a money word. The junk slips through.
strings.take.card: I built a junk filter today. It adds up clues into a score and compares it with a line. It never understands the message.

context: Strings from 'How does a junk filter decide?'. Learners sort messages, set three sliders (exclamation marks 1 point, money words 2, urgent words 3), apply the rule 'score 10 or more goes to junk' by hand, then try to fool the filter. {name} are ICU placeholders; <term-x> tags open a glossary definition.

clue.definition: कोई छोटा-सा संकेत जो कुछ तय करने में मदद करता है, जैसे संदेश में कोई शब्द या चिह्न

score.definition: अंकों को जोड़कर बनी एक संख्या

threshold.definition: एक रेखा जिस तक किसी संख्या को पहुँचना होता है; उस पर या उससे ऊपर एक बात होती है, नीचे दूसरी

training.definition: वह तरीका जिससे कोई प्रोग्राम बहुत सारे उदाहरणों से अपनी सेटिंग ख़ुद निकालता है, बजाय इसके कि कोई इंसान उन्हें हाथ से तय करे

filter.definition: कोई चीज़ जो कुछ चीज़ों को आगे जाने देती है और कुछ को रोक लेती है

junk.definition: ऐसे संदेश जो आपने नहीं माँगे, जैसे विज्ञापन और धोखे, जिन्हें आपके मुख्य संदेशों से अलग रखा जाता है

program.definition: सटीक कदमों की एक सूची, जिसका कंप्यूटर पालन करता है

inbox.definition: वह जगह जहाँ आपके चाहे हुए संदेश आते हैं

clue.definition: ఏదైనా నిర్ణయించడానికి సహాయపడే చిన్న సూచన, సందేశంలోని ఒక పదం లేదా గుర్తు లాంటిది

threshold.definition: ఒక సంఖ్య చేరాల్సిన గీత; దాని మీద లేదా పైన ఒకటి జరుగుతుంది, కింద మరొకటి

training.definition: ఒక మనిషి చేత్తో పెట్టే బదులు, ఒక ప్రోగ్రామ్ చాలా ఉదాహరణల నుండి తన సెట్టింగ్‌లను తానే లెక్కించుకునే విధానం

filter.definition: కొన్నింటిని ముందుకు పోనిచ్చి, కొన్నింటిని ఆపే ఏదైనా

junk.definition: మీరు అడగని సందేశాలు, ప్రకటనలు, మోసాలు లాంటివి; వీటిని మీ ముఖ్య సందేశాల నుండి వేరుగా ఉంచుతారు

audience.label: School learners, classes 8-12
audience.pacing: short loops; visible response within 1 second; mini-cycle within 3 minutes
